scope.status: review and positive ordinary census evidence; no allocation change implemented
observations: Fifteen vector lengths and three interpreted closure widths have identical GNU/Emaxx vector-slot census deltas after explicit collection. Changing the Lisp census to count 16-byte padding would introduce a difference.

Emaxx alloc/vectors.rs rounds allocation footprints to 16 bytes. Value tags use three low bits, and VectorlikeRef::allocate statically requires every generic payload alignment to be at most the eight-byte word size.
GNU alloc.c derives its vector rounding from object/word alignment; ordinary source-matched GNU reports unrounded word counts for the probed sizes.
ClosureRef currently charges rounded storage to the GC allocation counter. Six visible slots charge 64 bytes here, while GNU allocate_vectorlike tallies 56 logical bytes.
scope.proposed_next_change: Test one-word vector allocation granularity, preserving header layout and existing bitmap/large-mark ownership. Verify physical footprints, free-list splitting, bitmap boundaries, survival and reclamation, native ABI and image restoration. Do not alter the already-matching Lisp census merely to account for Rust padding.
scope.qualification: Static layout calculations and ordinary semantic control only. Physical allocation instrumentation, candidate runtime checks and performance measurements are still required. No source199 candidate exists yet.
